title: Antibiotics: Mechanisms and Types
text: Antibiotics are classified by their mechanism of action: cell wall synthesis inhibitors (beta-lactams like penicillin and cephalosporins, glycopeptides like vancomycin), protein synthesis inhibitors (macrolides, tetracyclines, aminoglycosides), DNA/RNA synthesis inhibitors (fluoroquinolones, rifamycins), and cell membrane disruptors (polymyxins). Broad-spectrum antibiotics act against many bacterial species, while narrow-spectrum antibiotics target specific organisms. The minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) is the lowest antibiotic concentration that prevents visible bacterial growth. Bactericidal antibiotics kill bacteria, while bacteriostatic antibiotics inhibit growth without killing. Antibiotic choice depends on the identified pathogen, its resistance pattern, and patient factors.
